judgments.rationale: Subsection (d)(5) provides an express governing limitation on access under this section, specifying that nothing in the section allows an individual access to information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding. Proposal P0000 properly incorporates this governing exception into the summary and context quotes to make the reading independently complete and accurate.

Proposal P0001 incorrectly asserts that the agency must require every individual, whether accompanied or unaccompanied, to furnish written authorization before access. Under the source text, furnishing a written statement authorizing discussion in an accompanying person's presence is an optional agency permission ('the agency may require') applicable specifically when an individual chooses to be accompanied.

The unchanged draft omits the governing statutory condition set forth in subsection (d)(5), which explicitly restricts access under this section for information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding. Because this governing restriction is omitted, the unchanged reading is incomplete for independent use.

source_spans.quote:
(d) Access to Records.— Each agency that maintains a system of rec­ords shall—

(1) upon request by any individual to gain access to his record or to any information pertaining to him which is contained in the system, permit him and upon his request, a person of his own choosing to accompany him, to review the record and have a copy made of all or any portion thereof in a form comprehensible to him, except that the agency may require the individual to furnish a written statement authorizing discussion of that individual’s record in the accompanying person’s presence;
(5) nothing in this section shall allow an individual access to any information compiled in reasonable anticipation of a civil action or proceeding.
